draft.title: The standard normal distribution
card: The standard normal variable Z has mean 0 and standard deviation 1. Any normal variable X with mean μ and standard deviation σ can be turned into Z.
The rule is Z = (X − μ)/σ. Subtract the mean, then divide by the standard deviation.
The value of Z says how many standard deviations X is from the mean. It is negative below the mean and positive above it.
To go back, use X = μ + σZ. Example: if μ = 50 and σ = 4, then X = 58 gives Z = (58 − 50)/4 = 2. The probability Pr(X < 58) equals Pr(Z < 2).
draft.remember: Z counts standard deviations from the mean, so one table of Z serves every normal variable.

a.q: A machine fills bags with mass X grams, normal with mean 250 and standard deviation 8. What is Z for a bag of 234 g?
a.why: Z = (234 − 250)/8 = −16/8 = −2. The value −16 is only the top line: it skips the division by the standard deviation.
a.clue: Subtract the mean first, then divide.

b.q: Daniel's bus journey time X, in minutes, is normal with mean 40 and standard deviation 6. One trip has a Z value of 1.5. How long did the trip take?
b.why: X = μ + σZ = 40 + 6 × 1.5 = 49. A positive Z means above the mean, so 31 is wrong. The value 41.5 adds Z without multiplying by σ.
b.clue: Z is a number of standard deviations. Turn it into minutes before adding.

final.title: The standard normal distribution
card: The standard normal variable \(Z\) has mean 0 and standard deviation 1. Any normal variable \(X\) with mean \(\mu\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\) can be turned into \(Z\).
The rule is \(Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}\). Subtract the mean, then divide by the standard deviation.
The value of \(Z\) says how many standard deviations \(X\) is from the mean. It is negative below the mean and positive above it.

To go back, use \(X = \mu + \sigma Z\). Example: if \(\mu = 50\) and \(\sigma = 4\), then \(X = 58\) gives \(Z = \frac{58 - 50}{4} = 2\). The probability \(\text{Pr}(X < 58)\) equals \(\text{Pr}(Z < 2)\).

4.alt: The standard normal curve for \(Z\), with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The area to the left of \(z = 2\) is shaded: it is \(\text{Pr}(Z < 2)\), the same as \(\text{Pr}(X < 58)\) when \(\mu = 50\) and \(\sigma = 4\).

final.remember: \(Z\) counts standard deviations from the mean, so a probability for \(X\) equals the matching probability for \(Z\).

a.q: A machine fills bags with mass \(X\) grams, normal with mean 250 and standard deviation 8. What is \(Z\) for a bag of 234 g?
a.why: \(Z = \frac{234 - 250}{8} = \frac{-16}{8} = -2\). The value \(-16\) is only the top line: it skips the division by the standard deviation. The bag is below the mean, so \(Z\) must be negative, which rules out 2.
a.clue: Subtract the mean first, then divide.

b.q: Daniel's bus journey time \(X\), in minutes, is normal with mean 40 and standard deviation 6. One trip has a \(Z\) value of 1.5. How long did the trip take?
b.why: \(X = \mu + \sigma Z = 40 + 6 \times 1.5 = 49\). A positive \(Z\) means above the mean, so 31 is wrong. The value 41.5 adds \(Z\) without multiplying by \(\sigma\), and 60 multiplies the mean by \(Z\).
b.clue: \(Z\) is a number of standard deviations. Turn it into minutes before adding.
